title: NY State Assembly · District 24
area: Central Queens, including Hollis, Jamaica Hills, Queens Village, Glen Oaks and parts of Richmond Hill and Jamaica.

context.text: Incumbent David Weprin advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after his only announced primary opponent, Mahtab Khan, was ruled off the ballot by the NYC Board of Elections for insufficient petition signatures. Welson Chang advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: David Weprin is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 24, which he has represented since winning a special election on February 9, 2010. A Queens native, he was a New York State deputy superintendent of banks in the 1980s, worked in financial services, and served on the New York City Council, where he chaired the Finance Committee. He chairs the Assembly Insurance Committee and also serves on the Banks, Codes, Judiciary and Ways and Means committees.

background.text: Born in Queens on May 2, 1956, to Saul and Sylvia Weprin, he has lived in the Hollis-Jamaica area his entire life, according to his official Assembly biography. He graduated from Jamaica High School.
Earned a B.A. in political science (cum laude) from the State University of New York at Albany and a law degree from Hofstra University.
In 1983, Gov. Mario Cuomo named him Deputy Superintendent of Banks and Secretary of the Banking Board for New York State, a position he held through 1987.

Held leadership positions at a major financial services firm from 1987 until his election to the City Council, and was elected by his peers as Chairman of the Securities Industry Association for the New York District for three years, according to his official biography.

Elected to the New York City Council from the 23rd Council District in Queens in 2001, and became chair of its Finance Committee within weeks of taking office; Ballotpedia says he chaired the committee for eight years. He did not seek re-election in 2009 and instead ran for City Comptroller; John Liu won that office.
Won a special election on February 9, 2010 to the Assembly's 24th District, the seat previously held by his father, the late Speaker Saul Weprin, and his brother Mark Weprin.
Ran in the September 2011 special election for New York's 9th Congressional District and lost to Republican Bob Turner, according to Wikipedia.

In the Assembly, was named chair of the Committee on Correction in 2017 and earlier chaired the Task Force on People with Disabilities (2014-2016); Ballotpedia lists him as chair of the Insurance Committee in the 2025-2026 session, alongside seats on the Banks, Codes, Judiciary, and Ways and Means committees. He was named co-president of the National Association of Jewish Legislators in January 2017.

According to his official biography, he lives in Holliswood with his wife, Ronni, and has five children, and he has been affiliated with civic and community organizations including the Holliswood Civic Association and the Greater Jamaica Development Corporation.

positions.summary: Sponsored a bill to delay the start of enforcement of the Manhattan central business district tolling program (congestion pricing) to no earlier than January 1, 2031, and issued a 2023 statement calling the program a "$1 Billion tax hike" on New Yorkers.
positions.quote: New Yorkers cannot afford this $1 Billion tax hike.

record.text: Chairs the Assembly Insurance Committee (2023-2026); also serves on the Banks, Codes, Judiciary, and Ways and Means committees.
Previously chaired the Assembly Correction Committee (2019-2022) and the Task Force on People with Disabilities.

Sponsored A01747, which would delay the start date of central business district tolling (congestion pricing) enforcement to no earlier than January 1, 2031; referred to the Transportation Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.
Sponsored A00303, establishing a New York State commission to end mass incarceration and prevent violence; referred to the Correction Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.

Sponsored A01723 (with co-sponsors including Nily Rozic), restricting municipalities from using funds to build or expand immigration detention facilities without legislative approval and creating an oversight committee; referred to the Local Governments Committee, not enacted as of January 2026.

candidates.name: Welson Chang

summary.text: Welson Chang is the Republican and Queens United Party nominee for NY State Assembly District 24, running against incumbent David Weprin. He describes himself as a small-business owner and naturalized U.S. citizen who founded a manufacturing business in 2020 after a decade in nonprofit administration, and has not previously held elected office. His campaign priorities include lowering taxes, supporting small businesses and keeping Regents exam requirements.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he graduated from Massena Central High School and earned a B.A. in history from McGill University (2000) and an M.S. in accountancy from the University of Phoenix (2020).
Describes himself as a naturalized U.S. citizen since 2008.
Says he spent a decade in nonprofit administration before entering the private sector in 2013, and founded a manufacturing business in 2020.
Became a county committee member in 2022, according to his survey, and says he serves on the boards of the Queens Village Republican Club and the Hollis Court at Bayside Coop.

Member of the Queens Village Republican Club; not formally endorsed by the Queens County Republican Party as of April 2026. He advanced to the general election without a primary after the June 23 Republican primary was canceled.
Spoke at Queens Village Republican Club events in Bayside and Alley Pond Park during the 2026 campaign.

priorities.text: Outlined campaign priorities centered on lowering taxes, supporting small businesses, and strengthening education standards.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, or FEC/OpenSecrets campaign-finance filing could be located as of this research date. Checked https://ballotpedia.org/Welson_Chang (survey not completed, no finance data), https://queenseagle.com/all/2026/4/30/two-queens-dem-mainstays-to-run-unopposed-after-challengers-booted-from-ballot, and news coverage of Queens Village Republican Club events (https://qns.com/2026/05/queens-village-republican-club-bayside-meeting/, https://qns.com/2026/08/barbecues-queens-republicans-america-250/), which describe his general campaign priorities but do not document specific positions on the guide's issue statements. Re-checked Oct. 19, 2026: Vote411 shows no responses from him; a Queens Village Republican Club page about his campaign was behind a bot-check and could not be read, and he has no campaign site that could be found. No verbatim statements on the guide's issues were available, so none were added.

researchNotes: Weprin's record draws on official NY Assembly bill pages. Two floor-vote claims (S10113, S3460) were removed on verification: the cited Assembly bill pages show only referral/passage actions, not the individual member's vote or the floor tally, and that data could not be confirmed from any reachable source. Chang has almost no independently verifiable public record; his entry reflects that. Chang's biography comes from his own 2026 Ballotpedia survey; no campaign website or news profile was found.
